questions.question_text: Rice grains take the shape of a jar container. Are they solid or liquid? Explain.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Rice grains are solids. Each individual grain retains its fixed shape and volume. They flow collectively only because they are small individual solid particles.

questions.question_text: Explain thermal expansion in metals using particle theory.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Heating supplies thermal kinetic energy, causing constituent metal particles to vibrate more vigorously around fixed positions. Increased vibration pushes particles slightly further apart, expanding macro dimensions.

questions.question_text: Explain phase transformations from ice to water to steam using kinetic particle theory.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: In ice (solid), particles vibrate in fixed grid positions bound by strong forces. Heating supplies thermal kinetic energy; at melting point (0 deg C), energy overcomes rigid attraction to form liquid water with mobile particles. Continued heating raises kinetic energy until boiling point (100 deg C), where particles break free completely into steam gas.

questions.question_text: Explain the principle of 7.2 States of Matter and Thermal Transitions and state its scientific significance.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Solids have minimal interparticle space and maximum attraction. Liquids have moderate spacing and fluidity. Gases have maximum spacing and free kinetic motion. Heating increases kinetic energy, causing phase transitions. questions.question_text: Explain the principle of 7.1 Particle Model of Matter and state its scientific significance.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Grinding chalk stick into fine powder demonstrates discrete sub-microscopic building particles. Particles possess interparticle spaces and mutual attractive forces. [Think like a scientist: Discrete vs Continuous] Matter looks continuous to human eyes, but physical behavior proves it is discrete and particulate.
